q: How many days of paternity leave do I get for a baby born in August 2025?
answer: You are entitled to 10 Working Days of paternity leave for a baby born in August 2025 [S1][S2].
standalone_query: How many days of paternity leave do I get for a baby born in August 2025?
follow_ups: Can the leave be taken in multiple spells?

citations.label: Leave Policy, p. 15, Circular HR/CIR/2025/07
citations.snippet: With effect from 1 July 2025, paternity leave under Clause 6.4.1 is increased from 5 Working Days to 10 Working Days, to be availed within six months of the date of birth or adoption.

citations.label: Leave Policy, p. 7, cl. 6.4.1
citations.snippet: 6.4.1 A male Employee is entitled to paternity leave of 5 Working Days on the birth of his child or on legally adopting a child below one year of age, to be availed within three months of the date of birth or adoption.

conflicts.reason: Circular HR/CIR/2025/07 amends 6.4.1, 6.4.2 with effect from 2025-07-01; the circular prevails from that date.

q: My father passed away last week. How many days of bereavement leave can I take?
answer: You are entitled to 5 Working Days of bereavement leave, to be taken within 15 Calendar Days of the death [S3][S2].

q: My salary for August has still not been credited. What should I do?
answer: Salary is credited on the last Working Day of each month, and any payroll issues should be raised as a ticket in the Payroll category within 30 days of the pay date; the team will correct it in the next payroll cycle [S2].
standalone_query: My salary for August has still not been credited. What should I do?
follow_ups: How can I check the exact pay date for this month?
What information should I include in the payroll ticket?
Will the correction affect my next month's salary?

citations.label: Compensation and Benefits Policy, p. 5, cl. 4.2
citations.snippet: An Employee who believes the payslip is incorrect raises a ticket in the Payroll category within 30 days; corrections are made in the next payroll.

q: A colleague keeps making jokes about my caste in team meetings.
answer: You can raise a complaint about the caste‑based jokes with the Internal Committee, or first speak confidentially to the HR Business Partner for guidance. Such remarks are prohibited as discrimination under the Code of Conduct and Ethics and qualify as harassment under the POSH policy’s definition of humiliating treatment that can affect health or safety [S8][S5][S6]. A grievance should be reported within 30 days of the incident, though the Internal Committee may consider extensions in special circumstances [S8][S2].

follow_ups: How do I file a written complaint with the Internal Committee?
